youtube.title: The First Thanksgiving Probably Had No Turkey
youtube.description:
Almost everything we know about the 1621 Plymouth harvest feast comes from one letter by Edward Winslow: four men went fowling, Massasoit arrived with about 90 men who killed five deer, and they feasted for three days. The only foods we can be sure of are venison and wild fowl; turkey is never mentioned. The Pilgrims didn't wear buckles, Winslow never called it "Thanksgiving" (the name was attached in the 1840s), and it became a national holiday in 1863 after years of letters from editor Sarah Josepha Hale.

Myths you were taught in school, Part 1. Which Thanksgiving myth did you grow up with?
